senses.gloss:
kuhū
------------------------------------------
Religious rites must always be performed on certain days considered as good and auspicious. Similarly, they should be avoided on inauspicious days.
According to the smṛtis and the पुराणस् the sage अङ्गिरस् begot four daughters from his wife स्मृति. They were: अनुमति, सिनीवाली, कुहू and राका. They were considered as the goddesses associated with certain phases of the मोओन् producing good or evil results.
Kuhū is the goddess associated with the new-मोओन् day mixed with the (next) first day of the bright fortnight. If, in addition, the प्लनेत्स् राहु, सूर्य (Sun), शनि (Saturn) and कुज (Mars) in the zodiacal sign मकर (Capricorn) get assembled, it is called Kuhūyoga.
The Kuhūyoga, though it may occur once in centuries, is considered as an extremely inauspicious moment, dangerous, or even fatal, for the rulers.
It is said that this occurred during the reign of Kṛṣṇadeva Rāya (A. D. 1488-1529) (the famous ruler of the Vijayanagar kingdom) and that he was saved by the Mādhva sage Vyāsarāya (A. D. 1447-1539).
